Namespace: [Ankus](/api/ankus/)

Assembly: `Ankus.Runtime.dll`

Names a column by which a custom scan path returns its rows in order.

```csharp
public readonly struct PgCustomScanSortKey : IEquatable<PgCustomScanSortKey>
```

Values compare as the default B-tree operator class of the column's type orders them, with the column's collation,
as <code>ORDER BY</code> on the column would. PostgreSQL trusts the order: rows out of order give wrong query results, as a
corrupt index would.

Implements: [IEquatable&lt;PgCustomScanSortKey&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.iequatable-1)

### PgCustomScanSortKey(int, bool, bool)

Names a column by which a custom scan path returns its rows in order.

```csharp
public PgCustomScanSortKey(int Ordinal, bool Descending, bool NullsFirst)
```

Parameters:

`Ordinal` — [int](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.int32)

The column's zero-based position in [Descriptor](/api/ankus.pgcustomscanplanner/#member-2f62b81003040c8b).

`Descending` — [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether larger values come first.

`NullsFirst` — [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether SQL NULL comes before every value.

Values compare as the default B-tree operator class of the column's type orders them, with the column's collation,
as <code>ORDER BY</code> on the column would. PostgreSQL trusts the order: rows out of order give wrong query results, as a
corrupt index would.
